attribution.note: Marcus wrote these words himself in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the hedge 'appears' on the moat clause and keeps the firm 'nobody has a solid answer' clause. It correctly treats both as observations about March 2025. 'LLM companies' is a fair reading of 'nobody'.

contract.note: The moat clause is hedged. 'Solid answer' has no reliability threshold or task scope, so any pass/fail test would add criteria Marcus did not supply. The contract fairly declines to set a binary test and does not invent a plain-reading measure.

evidence.note: A preprint dated 2025-03-20 finds over-reasoning and failures in several reasoning models. This is relevant background, but it uses no agreed 'solid answer' standard and does not cover every provider.
Anthropic's own February 2025 post describes reasoning improvements from test-time compute. It is a company statement about itself, and it shows neither a moat nor a solid answer to hallucinations.

reviews.rationale: The moat clause is hedged by 'appears'. The firm clause turns on 'solid answer', which has no threshold, tasks, or reliability standard, so it cannot be scored without inventing criteria. The evidence shows ongoing limitations and some attempts to improve, but it is context only and cannot settle the claim either way.
